Political Risk 
●
Corruption Scandals
○
2015: 1MDB scandal exposed, implicating then-Prime Minister Najib Razak.
○
2018: Najibʼs Barisan Nasional coalition defeated after 60+ years of rule.
○
2020: Najib convicted of corruption (12 years), sentence reduced to 6 years 
in 2024.
●
Leadership Changes
○
2020: Mahathir Mohamad resigns; replaced by Muhyiddin Yassin.
○
2021: Muhyiddin steps down; Ismail Sabri Yaakob assumes role.
○
2022: First-ever hung parliament resolved with Anwar Ibrahim as Prime 
Minister.
●
COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated governance challenges.

Economic Freedom
●
Trends in Economic Freedom
○
2018: Peak economic freedom score of 75/100.
○
2023-2024: Declined to 67 and 66, reflecting policy and economic challenges.
○
Score remains above global average of 59, indicating a relatively free economy.
●
Regional Competitiveness
○
Second in Southeast Asia, behind Singapore (84 in 2023).
○
Outperforms Indonesia (64) and Thailand (61) in regional rankings.
●
Strengths
○
Relatively open and competitive economy within the region.
○
High rankings highlight Malaysiaʼs economic liberalization and market openness.
●
Challenges
○
Recent score declines signal areas for reform:
■
Regulatory efficiency: Simplify business processes and reduce red tape.
■
Rule of law: Strengthen legal frameworks and property rights.
■
Open markets: Enhance trade liberalization and reduce trade barriers.

CPI
The Corruption Perceptions Index(CPI) ranks 180 countries by their perceived levels of public 
sector corruption, scoring on a scale of 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean).
Malaysia has a score of 50 this year and ranks 57th out of 180 countries.

Corruption in Malaysia 
Bribery and Kickbacks 
Embezzlement 
Abuse of Power
The Malaysian government has made efforts to tackle corruption, including launching the National 
Anti-Corruption Strategy to strengthen governance and promote integrity. However, addressing these 
entrenched issues requires systemic reforms.

Governance: Monarchy & Executive 
Constitutional Monarchy:
●
Malaysia uses a unique monarchy system. There system features a rotating monarchy, 
where one of the nine hereditary state rulers serves as the King (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) 
for a five-year term. The Kingʼs role is mainly ceremonial.
Executive Branch:
●
The Prime Minister-is the Head of Government, leading the executive branch and holding 
significant authority.
●
Cabinets- The Prime Minister forms the Cabinet, which consists of ministers responsible 
for various portfolios (e.g., finance, health, education).

Governance: Legislative & Judicial 
Legislative Branch: 
●
House of Representatives (Dewan Rakyat)- is composed of 222 members elected 
by the people. Members serve five-year terms.
●
Senate (Dewan Negara)- is composed of 70 members, some appointed by state 
legislatures and other by the King. 
Judicial Branch:
●
The judiciary is independent and based on English common law: There courts 
consist of:
○
Federal Court (highest court)
○
Court of Appeal
○
High Courts 
○
Subordinate courts
